Source format: Meeting minutes and bylaws

1. Welcome and opening remarks
Mr. Sridhar welcomed all residents and thanked them for their participation. He explained
that the purpose of forming the Union was to create a collective platform for addressing
common issues such as maintenance of common areas, security, water supply, and
coordination with the BBMP and BWSSB. He noted that the formation committee had been
working since January 2018 and had prepared the draft bylaws after two consultation
meetings.

2. Adoption of the draft bylaws
The draft bylaws, circulated to all members on 5 April 2018, were read out clause by clause.
After discussion, the following amendments were proposed and adopted:

- Clause 7(b): The term of the Executive Committee shall be two years instead of one
  year, to ensure continuity of ongoing projects.
- Clause 12: The quorum for the Annual General Body Meeting shall be one-third of the
  total registered members, instead of the earlier proposed one-half.
- Clause 15: A sub-committee may co-opt up to two non-member residents as invitees,
  subject to the approval of the EC.

The draft bylaws, with the above amendments, were put to vote. The resolution was passed
unanimously with 47 votes in favour and none against. The bylaws shall come into force
with effect from the date of this meeting.

RESOLUTION No. 1/2018: Adopted the bylaws of the Indiranagar Dwelling Union as
amended above.

3. Election of the Executive Committee
The following members were elected unanimously by a show of hands:

- President: Mr. K. R. Sridhar
- Vice-President: Mrs. Meera Raghavan
- Secretary: Mr. Anil Kumar
- Joint Secretary: Mr. Prakash Rao
- Treasurer: Mrs. Sunita Deshpande
- EC Members (3): Mr. Ravi Shankar, Mrs. Lakshmi Venkatesh, Mr. Joseph Thomas

The elected members took charge with immediate effect. The Secretary was authorised to
open a bank account in the name of the Union with the State Bank of India, Indiranagar
Branch.

4. Fixing the annual membership fee
The formation committee proposed an annual membership fee of Rs. 500 per household,
payable by 30th April each year. After discussion on the need for a corpus fund for
emergency repairs and legal expenses, the General Body unanimously approved the
proposal.

RESOLUTION No. 2/2018: The annual membership fee shall be Rs. 500 per household,
payable by 30th April each year. The fee shall be reviewed annually by the Executive
Committee.

5. Formation of sub-committees
The General Body resolved to form the following sub-committees:

According to the IDU minutes and bylaws, the Indiranagar Dwelling Union founded_on is 2018-04-15. Record status: current.

a) Maintenance and Infrastructure Sub-Committee – to liaise with BBMP, BWSSB, and
   BESCOM on civic issues, and to oversee maintenance of common areas.
   Convener: Mr. Ravi Shankar

b) Security Sub-Committee – to coordinate with the local police station and private
   security agencies, and to review the deployment of security guards.
   Convener: Mr. Joseph Thomas

c) Grievance Redressal Sub-Committee – to receive and resolve complaints from
   members regarding common facilities and neighbourly disputes.
   Convener: Mrs. Lakshmi Venkatesh

d) Cultural and Social Sub-Committee – to organise festivals, sports events, and
   community gatherings.
   Convener: Mrs. Meera Raghavan

Each sub-committee shall have 3 to 5 members, to be nominated by the EC within 15 days.
The sub-committees shall report to the EC at each monthly meeting.

RESOLUTION No. 3/2018: Formation of the four sub-committees as listed above, with the
named conveners, and the EC authorised to fill the remaining member positions.

6. Any other matter
- Mr. Sridhar informed the members that the Union would register itself under the
  Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, and the registration formalities would be
  completed within two months.
- It was decided to hold the General Body Meeting once every three months, and the
  EC meeting once a month on the first Sunday.

The meeting concluded with a vote of thanks by the Joint Secretary, Mr. Prakash Rao.

**Item 4 – Amendment to Bylaw 12 – Legal Cell Meeting Frequency**

This item was the primary agenda for the meeting. The Legal Cell was constituted in July 2019 to handle matters relating to the pending litigation with the builder regarding the undivided share of land and also to advise the association on property tax matters and rental agreements for the community hall.

**Background:** Bylaw 12 as originally framed (2018) stated that the Legal Cell shall meet "once every two months or as and when required." In practice, the cell met irregularly in 2019–2020, with only 4 meetings held between July 2019 and October 2020. The last meeting was on 12 September 2020.

**Proposal:** The Executive Committee proposed an amendment to Bylaw 12 to fix a regular meeting frequency. Two options were placed before the general body:

**Option A (proposed by the Executive Committee):** The Legal Cell shall meet once every three months (quarterly), with provision for additional meetings as and when required.

**Option B (moved by Mr. S. Prakash, seconded by Mrs. R. Shobha):** The Legal Cell shall meet once every month (monthly). Mr. Prakash argued that the pending litigation requires closer monitoring, and that a monthly meeting would ensure the cell remains actively engaged with the advocate and the court dates.

**Discussion:** Several members spoke in support of Option A. Mr. R. Venkatesh (President) noted that the cell's role is advisory and that monthly meetings would place an undue burden on the four cell members, all of whom have full-time jobs. Mrs. Kamala R, a cell member, stated that quarterly meetings, supplemented by written updates from the advocate via email, would be sufficient. She also noted that the cell can convene an emergency meeting at short notice if a court date or legal notice requires it.

Mr. Prakash, in response, stated that the builder's counsel had filed an additional written statement in October 2020, and that the cell needed to review documents more frequently. The President clarified that the amendment fixes the minimum regular frequency; nothing prevents the cell from meeting more often if the convenor deems it necessary.

**Voting:** A show of hands was taken. 64 members voted in favour of Option A (quarterly), 31 voted in favour of Option B (monthly), and 4 abstained. Option A carried with the required two-thirds majority.

**Resolution No. 2020/11/04:** Bylaw 12 is hereby amended. The amended text reads as follows:

> **Bylaw 12 – Legal Cell.** There shall be a Legal Cell consisting of not less than three and not more than five members of the association, appointed by the Executive Committee. The Legal Cell shall advise the association on legal matters, including but not limited to litigation, contracts, and regulatory compliance. The Legal Cell shall meet once every three months (quarterly), or more frequently as and when required by the convenor or by the Executive Committee. The convenor shall circulate the minutes of each meeting to the Executive Committee within seven days of the meeting. The Legal Cell shall report to the General Body at the Annual General Meeting.

documents.title: IDU Minutes and Bylaws
documents.content:
1. Welcome and opening remarks
Mr. Sridhar welcomed all residents and thanked them for their participation. He explained
that the purpose of forming the Union was to create a collective platform for addressing
common issues such as maintenance of common areas, security, water supply, and
coordination with the BBMP and BWSSB. He noted that the formation committee had been
working since January 2018 and had prepared the draft bylaws after two consultation
meetings.

2. Adoption of the draft bylaws
The draft bylaws, circulated to all members on 5 April 2018, were read out clause by clause.
After discussion, the following amendments were proposed and adopted:

- Clause 7(b): The term of the Executive Committee shall be two years instead of one
  year, to ensure continuity of ongoing projects.
- Clause 12: The quorum for the Annual General Body Meeting shall be one-third of the
  total registered members, instead of the earlier proposed one-half.
- Clause 15: A sub-committee may co-opt up to two non-member residents as invitees,
  subject to the approval of the EC.

The draft bylaws, with the above amendments, were put to vote. The resolution was passed
unanimously with 47 votes in favour and none against. The bylaws shall come into force
with effect from the date of this meeting.

RESOLUTION No. 1/2018: Adopted the bylaws of the Indiranagar Dwelling Union as
amended above.

3. Election of the Executive Committee
The following members were elected unanimously by a show of hands:

- President: Mr. K. R. Sridhar
- Vice-President: Mrs. Meera Raghavan
- Secretary: Mr. Anil Kumar
- Joint Secretary: Mr. Prakash Rao
- Treasurer: Mrs. Sunita Deshpande
- EC Members (3): Mr. Ravi Shankar, Mrs. Lakshmi Venkatesh, Mr. Joseph Thomas

The elected members took charge with immediate effect. The Secretary was authorised to
open a bank account in the name of the Union with the State Bank of India, Indiranagar
Branch.

4. Fixing the annual membership fee
The formation committee proposed an annual membership fee of Rs. 500 per household,
payable by 30th April each year. After discussion on the need for a corpus fund for
emergency repairs and legal expenses, the General Body unanimously approved the
proposal.

RESOLUTION No. 2/2018: The annual membership fee shall be Rs. 500 per household,
payable by 30th April each year. The fee shall be reviewed annually by the Executive
Committee.

5. Formation of sub-committees
The General Body resolved to form the following sub-committees:

According to the IDU minutes and bylaws, the Indiranagar Dwelling Union founded_on is 2018-04-15. Record status: current.

a) Maintenance and Infrastructure Sub-Committee – to liaise with BBMP, BWSSB, and
   BESCOM on civic issues, and to oversee maintenance of common areas.
   Convener: Mr. Ravi Shankar

b) Security Sub-Committee – to coordinate with the local police station and private
   security agencies, and to review the deployment of security guards.
   Convener: Mr. Joseph Thomas

c) Grievance Redressal Sub-Committee – to receive and resolve complaints from
   members regarding common facilities and neighbourly disputes.
   Convener: Mrs. Lakshmi Venkatesh

d) Cultural and Social Sub-Committee – to organise festivals, sports events, and
   community gatherings.
   Convener: Mrs. Meera Raghavan

Each sub-committee shall have 3 to 5 members, to be nominated by the EC within 15 days.
The sub-committees shall report to the EC at each monthly meeting.

RESOLUTION No. 3/2018: Formation of the four sub-committees as listed above, with the
named conveners, and the EC authorised to fill the remaining member positions.

6. Any other matter
- Mr. Sridhar informed the members that the Union would register itself under the
  Karnataka Societies Registration Act, 1960, and the registration formalities would be
  completed within two months.
- It was decided to hold the General Body Meeting once every three months, and the
  EC meeting once a month on the first Sunday.

The meeting concluded with a vote of thanks by the Joint Secretary, Mr. Prakash Rao.

Mr. Anil Kumar
Secretary, IDU

Mr. Dinesh Kumar, Maintenance Committee member, reported that the lift in Tower B has been out of service since 2 November. Vendor quote for repair of the motor: ₹48,500. Two other quotes obtained: ₹52,000 and ₹46,800. The committee recommended accepting the lowest quote from M/s Sri Balaji Elevators. **Item 3 – Financial Statement – October 2020**

Treasurer presented the statement:

The statement was approved. Mrs. Usha R asked about the delay in issuing receipts for October maintenance. Treasurer clarified that receipts were generated on 5 November due to printer issues; all members have since received them via WhatsApp and email.

---

The IDU minutes and bylaws state that the IDU Legal Cell meeting_frequency_months is 3 months. Record status: current.

**Item 4 – Amendment to Bylaw 12 – Legal Cell Meeting Frequency**

This item was the primary agenda for the meeting. The Legal Cell was constituted in July 2019 to handle matters relating to the pending litigation with the builder regarding the undivided share of land and also to advise the association on property tax matters and rental agreements for the community hall.

**Background:** Bylaw 12 as originally framed (2018) stated that the Legal Cell shall meet "once every two months or as and when required." In practice, the cell met irregularly in 2019–2020, with only 4 meetings held between July 2019 and October 2020. The last meeting was on 12 September 2020.

**Proposal:** The Executive Committee proposed an amendment to Bylaw 12 to fix a regular meeting frequency. Two options were placed before the general body:

**Option A (proposed by the Executive Committee):** The Legal Cell shall meet once every three months (quarterly), with provision for additional meetings as and when required.

**Option B (moved by Mr. S. Prakash, seconded by Mrs. R. Shobha):** The Legal Cell shall meet once every month (monthly). Mr. Prakash argued that the pending litigation requires closer monitoring, and that a monthly meeting would ensure the cell remains actively engaged with the advocate and the court dates.

**Discussion:** Several members spoke in support of Option A. Mr. R. Venkatesh (President) noted that the cell's role is advisory and that monthly meetings would place an undue burden on the four cell members, all of whom have full-time jobs. Mrs. Kamala R, a cell member, stated that quarterly meetings, supplemented by written updates from the advocate via email, would be sufficient. She also noted that the cell can convene an emergency meeting at short notice if a court date or legal notice requires it.

Mr. Prakash, in response, stated that the builder's counsel had filed an additional written statement in October 2020, and that the cell needed to review documents more frequently. The President clarified that the amendment fixes the minimum regular frequency; nothing prevents the cell from meeting more often if the convenor deems it necessary.

**Voting:** A show of hands was taken. 64 members voted in favour of Option A (quarterly), 31 voted in favour of Option B (monthly), and 4 abstained. Option A carried with the required two-thirds majority.

**Resolution No. 2020/11/04:** Bylaw 12 is hereby amended. The amended text reads as follows:

> **Bylaw 12 – Legal Cell.** There shall be a Legal Cell consisting of not less than three and not more than five members of the association, appointed by the Executive Committee. The Legal Cell shall advise the association on legal matters, including but not limited to litigation, contracts, and regulatory compliance. The Legal Cell shall meet once every three months (quarterly), or more frequently as and when required by the convenor or by the Executive Committee. The convenor shall circulate the minutes of each meeting to the Executive Committee within seven days of the meeting. The Legal Cell shall report to the General Body at the Annual General Meeting.
